newsitem.title: UK: U.S stocks in London slightly up, await ECI data.
newsitem.headline: U.S stocks in London slightly up, await ECI data.

text.p: U.S. shares were moderately higher on Tuesday but trading volume was light as investors awaited key Employment Cost Index (ECI) data, due at 1235 GMT.

The ECI, which measures both wages and benefits and is closely watched by the U.S. Federal Reserve as a star indicator on inflation, is forecast to rise by 0.9 percent in the first quarter after a 0.8 percent increase the previous period.
"A big jump in the ECI would certainly raise expectations of a Fed rate hike next month," one senior dealer said. "Anything above 1.0 percent and it could be a bad day for bonds and the Dow."
Wall Street's 44-point advance on Monday, which ended a three-day losing streak, encouraged some selective buying in Europe.

Boeing Co, which plunged $6-3/4 on Monday after its first-quarter figures disappointed the market, was up $3/8 to $95-5/8. "We've seen a bit of bargain hunting which is hardly surprising after yesterday's hit," a market maker said.

He said Boeing's gains in Europe were "tempered" by a report in Tuesday's New York Times newspaper which said a strategic defence review by the Pentagon could lead to lower Air Force and Navy budgets for high-technology jet aircraft, including the F-22 fighter.

The F-22 programme is led by Lockheed Martin with Boeing a principal subcontractor, responsible for several key components including the manufacture of wings, radar, and mission software. The U.S. Airforce alone had planned to order 438 aircraft at a cost of $48 billion, according to Flight International magazine.
Elsewhere, PepsiCo Inc was up $1/8 to $31-3/8 ahead of its first quarter figures, due later on Tuesday.
IBM, which holds its annual shareholders meeting later today, was up $1/4 to $150-5/8.
